summary: Looks up a resource node in a linked list owned by this, in one of two modes selected by a3: when a3 != -1 it matches the node's integer ID field, and when a3 == -1 it matches the node's string name against a2 using sub_588410 (a string compare that returns 0 on a match). The list head is this[14] (offset 0x38); the traversal cursor this[16] (offset 0x40) is reset to the head on entry and advanced through each node's +4 next pointer per iteration. Returns the data pointer of the matching node, or 0 when the list is empty, the key is absent, or the list is exhausted.

local_names.a2: string key used in string-name mode
local_names.a3: integer ID key; -1 selects string-name mode
local_names.v4: data pointer of the current node

operations.description: Dual-mode dispatch on a3: when a3 != -1 the function matches on the integer ID; when a3 == -1 it matches on the string name in a2 (via sub_588410).
ID mode: reset the traversal cursor this[16] = this[14] (list head, offset 0x38); when the head is null return 0 immediately.

ID mode: iterate the list, advancing the cursor through each node's +4 next pointer (this[16] = *(node + 4)), comparing the resource ID at data+16 with a3 and returning the matching data pointer; return 0 when the next pointer is null before a match.
ID mode: return the data pointer of the matching node, or 0 when the list is empty or the ID is absent.
String mode: when a2 is non-null, reset the cursor this[16] = this[14] (list head); return 0 when the list is empty.

String mode: read the node's name string at data+4 (using the byte_5EA438 default string when the name pointer is null), call sub_588410(name, a2), and stop on a 0 return (match); otherwise advance the cursor through node->next and return 0 on exhaustion.
String mode: return the data pointer of the matching node, or 0 when a2 is null, the list is empty, or the name is absent.
